sentences.text: Ward staff perform a receipt check on each arriving load before placing medication in a cabinet or transferring custody.
A Registered Nurse or other authorized ward staff member verifies that the load is intended for the ward.
North Ward Cabinet Controller records the arrival time and the destination cabinet for loads assigned to the north ward.
South Ward Cabinet Controller records the arrival time and the destination cabinet for loads assigned to the south ward.
North Ward Cabinet Controller uses the Priority Refill Tote Tag to confirm the intended ward before staff accept a tote.
Staff inspect the outer packaging for damage, moisture, tampering, or other signs that the load may be unsafe to handle.
Ward staff compare package identifiers with the cabinet task list and confirm that the identifiers are legible.
Cabinet staff verify the quantity and medication descriptions against the expected receipt record.
For refrigerated medication, a Registered Nurse checks that the load remained within the required handling conditions.
Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler displays the current temperature and any recorded excursion for staff review.
Staff isolate a load when its identity, quantity, packaging, or temperature condition does not match the expected receipt.
Staff do not place an unresolved load into active cabinet stock.
Accepted medication is staged in the designated receiving area until cabinet placement is authorized.
The ward records receipt completion and any discrepancy through the established operational process.
Ward staff check return bins before use to confirm that each bin is intact, clean, and assigned to the correct return stream.
A Registered Nurse confirms that the contents are eligible for return and are separated from waste and non-medication items.
Staff check that each return bin closes securely and that its contents do not obstruct the closure.
Tallowmere guides ward staff through return-bin checks and records each check outcome for follow-up.
The Pharmacy Technician uses the audit label to identify a return bin for the scheduled collection.
Staff reconcile the bin contents with the return entry before the bin is closed.
Questionable or damaged returned medication is segregated and referred for review rather than combined with accepted returns.
A checked return bin remains secured in its designated holding location until collection is authorized.
The Hospital Courier collects only bins that are closed and recorded as ready for collection.
The Charge Nurse ensures that unresolved receipt or return discrepancies remain assigned for follow-up at shift handover.
